commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[skyrl] Keep turn terminators out of visible replies (#11845)

Replayed multi-turn histories contain an extra end-of-turn (EOT) token
inside each assistant tool-call turn, and this extra token reduces tool
use.

Since [#11232](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11232), the
SkyRL model client adds the trailing turn terminator back to reply text
when `skip_special_tokens=False`. The long-loop agent path uses that
setting, so each historical assistant message has an EOT before its tool
call. The chat template then adds a second EOT after the tool call. The
LongLoop round-4 audit found EOT tokens inside all 142 parsed tool-call
messages, and in none of 3,802 tool-call messages saved from round 1
([audit
evidence](s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/eot-history-fix/evidence/audit-evidence.json),
[Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Feot-history-fix%2Fevidence%2Faudit-evidence.json)).
On the frozen round-4 weights, removal of the two EOTs from a saved
BixBench prompt increased next tool calls from 1/8 to 8/8 over eight
matched seeds ([paired
replay](s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/eot-history-fix/2026.11.20.1/paired-summary.json),
[Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Feot-history-fix%2F2026.11.20.1%2Fpaired-summary.json)).
The effect on full-task scores is not measured.

When a reply ends its turn, its text (`responses` and assistant message
`content`) does not include the EOS or turn terminator, for completion,
assistant-prefix, and chat replies. Sampled `response_ids` do not
change, and `skip_special_tokens` controls only the special tokens
inside the reply.

The Marin chat template moves from `marin.datakit` to
`rolloutengine.chat_template`, because Marin and SkyRL both depend on
rolloutengine. The SkyRL history tests render with this template, so no
copy of the template is necessary. The template text does not change.

commits.message:
[loom] Send weekday Slack reminders for overdue PR reviews (#12145)

Loom posts a weekday digest of overdue individual review requests to
#marin-eng at 10:00 Pacific. Each entry links the PR and shows its
title, the time since its last update, and how long each requested
reviewer has been inactive.

A request is due when both the request and the reviewer’s latest
activity predate the same time on the previous weekday. The digest skips
drafts, PRs last updated more than seven days ago, and PRs from bots or
authors without repository write access. Empty scans stay quiet. Large
digests split at PR boundaries to fit Loom’s message limit.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[levanter] Remove checkpoint metadata before payload during pruning (#11718)

Remove `metadata.json` and check that it is absent before recursively
removing the checkpoint payload. If marker removal fails with an error
other than file-not-found, or the marker remains visible, skip payload
removal. An interrupted recursive prune can leave a discoverable
metadata marker over an incomplete payload. Hiding the marker first lets
subsequent discovery skip the prefix during payload removal.

This ordering does not protect a reader that already selected the
checkpoint before pruning started, and writes and deletes to a reused
step prefix still require serialization.

Part of #11714

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[evals] Add the MultiChallenge multi-turn benchmark (#11757)

Add `--evals multichallenge`, Scale AI's
[MultiChallenge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17399). Each item is a fixed
user/assistant conversation that ends on a user turn. The served model
writes only the final assistant reply. The data is the 266-row public
release,
[`ScaleAI/MultiChallenge`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/MultiChallenge)
at `670fd81f270314d0f8f82b34fcfe2187fd28f699`. The history is replayed
unchanged as chat messages, with no system prompt. A judge answers the
item's yes/no `target_question` from the final answer alone and passes
the item on `YES`. Scores are grouped by the four axes: inference memory
(109), instruction retention (69), self-coherence (48) and reliable
version editing (40). The judge is `openai/gpt-oss-120b` through
Together, bound as for the other judged evals. A second commit defines
that Together judge block once with a YAML anchor; the loaded
configuration is unchanged.

The judge prompt is Marin's own, written from the paper's description of
the judge without reference to the authors' runner prompt, which has no
license. The judge sees only the final reply and the item's question,
gives brief reasoning, and writes `YES` or `NO` alone on the final line.
Intended differences from the authors' runner:
- Marin's prompt replaces the runner's, which tells the judge to be
"VERY STRICT".
- gpt-oss-120b replaces `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`.
- Each model keeps its own sampling defaults instead of temperature 0.
- Only the final answer is graded, so reasoning never reaches the judge.
- `accuracy` is the item mean. The paper's headline, the mean of the
four axis accuracies, is in the table below.

Licensing: the dataset is CC-BY-4.0, and the judge prompt is written for
Marin.

Full runs, 266 items each, all items scored, no infrastructure errors,
graded with Marin's prompt:

| Model | Hardware | Accuracy ± SE | Axis mean | Truncated | Published |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | H100x4 | 71.8 ± 2.8 | 66.2 | 3 (1.1%) | 60.0, Qwen
model card; judge and population unstated |
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 67.3 ± 2.9 | 64.2 | 0 | none |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | H100x4 | 66.5 ± 2.9 | 64.1 | 0 | none |
| Snowball v0.1, `grug` parser | H100x8 | 49.2 ± 3.1 | 47.2 | 0 | none |

Qwen's axis mean is 2.1 standard errors above its card. The card does
not name its judge or dataset. We have not graded the Qwen responses
with the authors' GPT-4o judge. Snowball left 4 answers empty because
its reasoning never closed; they score 0.

All 266 compiled conversations matched the source rows byte for byte.
The full runs were first graded with the authors' runner prompt;
re-judging all 1,064 recorded responses with Marin's prompt raised each
model's score by 0.4-2.2 points (at most 0.8 standard errors) and kept
the ranking. Marin's prompt disagrees with itself on 3.3% of verdicts
across two passes, against 4.4% for the runner prompt, and returned no
malformed verdicts in 2,128 calls. Two independent language-model
reviewers, blind to every verdict, labeled the responses where the
prompts disagree, along with an earlier stratified sample of 87. On the
108 disagreements where the reviewers agree, Marin's prompt made 41
errors, the runner prompt 48 and a variant of Marin's prompt told to
apply requirements exactly 58. On the stratified sample, Marin's prompt
has an estimated error rate of 4.1% (95% CI 1.0-9.3%), the same as the
runner prompt; its errors split 25 false fails to 16 false passes on the
disagreements, where the runner prompt's split 38 to 10. Typical
remaining errors misread the response or follow from the judge not
seeing the conversation, which matches the authors' design.

Cost at CoreWeave list price, $6.155 per H100-hour:

| Run | Eval time | Worker start to finish | H100-hours | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer 30B | 9.0 min | 13.1 min | 0.44 | $2.69 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | 7.4 min | 13.8 min | 0.92 | $5.65 |
| Snowball v0.1 | 6.2 min | 9.4 min | 1.25 | $7.69 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 8.4 min | 14.0 min | 0.93 | $5.73 |

The judge used 0.78M input tokens over 1,064 calls, about $0.05 per
model; gpt-oss's hidden reasoning tokens are not recorded, so this is an
estimate. Run records are under
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/multichallenge-full-*-20261119-multichallenge-*`.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finelog] Release the policy mutex before eviction (#12035)

Eviction reads the storage policy through an accessor that releases the
policy
mutex before eviction waits for query readers. Before, a temporary guard
in the
eviction call kept the mutex locked for the whole call. During
[incident 1046](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1046), registration
waited
behind that mutex in a policy update, and 510 more registration requests
filled
the blocking pool.

The regression test holds a query reader, starts eviction, and requires
a policy
update to finish while eviction waits. With the fix reverted, the test
fails at
its 5-second timeout. The operations guide describes how to diagnose a
blocked
pod and what a container restart keeps.

Two hardening items from the issue are not in this change: a deadline
over the
whole forwarding read, including snapshot acquisition, and admission
control for
registration before it occupies blocking workers.

Part of #12024

commits.message:
[eval] Add GenomeQA through TaskCompendium (#10984)

Add the original 5,200-question GenomeQA benchmark through
TaskCompendium, using pinned Hugging Face data and an externally fetched
runner prompt. The existing evaluation pipeline publishes the corpus
with the converter and packaged grader versioned together. The GenomeQA
grader selects the last answer section, uses VerifyIt’s shared MCQ
parser to read the choice, and gives each of the twelve subtask × format
cells equal weight while retaining ordinary accuracy and grouped
diagnostics.

Use the served model’s decoding settings and the run’s output cap.
Require enough context for the full prompt and that cap. Grade the
available final answer. Archived model turns retain the provider stop
reason for reporting. Unparseable answers score zero.

Replaying all 31,200 saved answers from six full runs (temperature 0.7,
top-p 0.95, 16,384-token cap) with the shared parser and answer-section
selection reproduced the recorded answer choices and accuracy scores.
Native EvalDash reduction reproduced the six overall scores and their
subtask and format-cell breakdowns. See #10981 for results.

Part of #10981.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[evals] Add PHYSICS-Verified with a per-answer judge rubric (#11820)

Add `physics-verified`: the 602 test problems without figures from
[PHYSICS-Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yale-nlp/physics-verified)
@ `724170025e35`, the authors' audited release of
[PHYSICS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21821). The problems come from
physics PhD qualifying exams in six domains and carry 1,454 labelled
reference answers (861 symbolic, 459 numeric, 134 text); 60% ask for
more than one result. The system prompt and judge prompt are copied from
the release's harness (`eval/prompts.py`), which uses the Humanity's
Last Exam response format. One judge call per problem returns a yes/no
verdict for each reference answer. `accuracy` counts a problem only when
every answer is correct; each grade also records the fraction of correct
answers. The judge is GLM-5.3-Flash on Together, the authors' judge
model; it sees the final answer only. Scores are grouped by domain, and
the benchmark is in no suite. The dataset and harness are MIT-licensed.

The judge needs a new `answers` rubric in verifyit's judge mode: one
request returns a JSON object with one verdict per reference, and the
task scores 1 only when all are correct. It omits `temperature` so the
judge samples with its own defaults, as the harness does. At temperature
0, GLM-5.3-Flash spent its whole 32,768-token budget reasoning on 27 of
602 problems. A reply that exhausts 32,768 tokens is retried once with
65,536; both attempts fit inside the evaluator's 600 s grading timeout.
The `labels`, `reference` and `checklist` rubrics are unchanged.

The original PHYSICS harness scores each item as the fraction of the
model's boxed answers that match any reference, so one correct box on a
five-part question scores 1.0 (yale-nlp/Physics#4). The verified release
fixes that, removes 188 problems that need a proof or a missing figure,
and audits the reference answers.

Full runs on 2026-11-19, all on CoreWeave H100s in `cw-us-east-02a`:

| Model | Hardware | Scored | Accuracy | Truncated | Published |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| nvidia-nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b-bf16 | H100x4 | 602/602 | 85.1
± 1.5 | 33 | |
| muse-glimmer-30b | H100x2 | 597/602 | 84.6 ± 1.5 | 0 | |
| qwen3.5-122b-a10b-fp8, 73,728-token context | H100x8 | 602/602 | 76.6
± 1.7 | 16 | 80.9 (BF16, 95% CI 77.7–84.1) |
| Snowball v0.1 | H100x8 | 602/602 | 55.5 | 1 | |

Truncated responses score zero, as in the authors' table. Glimmer's 5
unscored problems are judge replies that exhausted both token budgets.
Qwen3.5-122B is 4.3 points (1.9 standard errors) below its published
score. Grading explains at most about 1 point of that gap: re-judging
the authors' own 602 published Qwen3.5-122B-A10B responses through this
pipeline gives 80.1 against their 80.9, with 96.7% agreement on
individual answers. The rest comes from generation: FP8 weights, 16
truncations, and fresh samples. The curated default judge, gpt-oss-120b,
agreed on 90.6% of answers and scored the same responses 68.9. In a
blind read of 11 disagreements, the authors' judge was right on 8; high
reasoning effort did not close the gap. All 602 compiled requests match
the harness's rendering of the system prompt, question and reference
list byte for byte.

| Run | Hardware | Eval time | Inference worker | GPU-hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer | H100x2 | 42 min | 47 min | 1.6 |
| Nemotron | H100x4 | 2.1 h | 2.2 h | 8.7 |
| Snowball | H100x8 | 34 min | 38 min | 5.0 |
| Qwen3.5-122B-FP8 | H100x8 | 3.8 h | 3.1 h, 4 preemptions | 24.6 |

Judge calls cost an estimated $3–6 per 602-problem run at Together's
$0.15/$0.50 per million tokens.

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model muse-glimmer-30b --evals physics-verified --priority interactive
```

commits.message: [serve] Make the serve dashboard usable on phones (#11682) Make the serve dashboard usable on phones (360–390px) and keep its toolbar from overflowing at tablet and narrow desktop widths. On the deployed dashboard at 390px, the chat toolbar was 622px wide, so the max tokens input and the More options button (temperature, system prompt) were off screen. The toolbar now sizes against the main column through a container query, because the history panel takes 256px of the screen from the `md` breakpoint up. When the column is at least 768px wide, max tokens is in the toolbar; below that it moves into the More options panel. Share and Report issue show text labels from 896px. If space still runs out, only the mode tabs scroll, so More options stays visible. At window widths of 768–1023px, max tokens sits in the toolbar for Compare (which has no history panel) and in the panel for Chat and Completion. On touch devices, form fields use 16px text so iOS Safari does not zoom on focus. Enter in the chat and compare composers inserts a newline because touch keyboards have no Shift+Enter; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends, and touch devices that also report a trackpad show that hint. The Compare URL row stacks on narrow screens so Connect no longer covers the input. Measured in Chrome and headless Chromium with feedback enabled, from 320px to 1512px: the toolbar fits at every width, and only the mode tabs scroll, at 320px. The touch-only behaviour has not been tried on a physical device. Chat view at 390px, before and after. Both captures are from desktop Chrome, so the composer still shows the desktop shortcut hint.

[tasks] Share task error types across framework category maps (#11812)

Copied error tables let training treatment drift between Harbor and
SkyRL.

Keep ErrorCategory and RetrySettings in Rigging with the map from shared
task and SDK error names to categories. Shellbox owns machine and
Daytona categories. Harbor owns its other native categories and the
policy for resuming trials in a new job. SkyRL composes these maps with
its own errors. It includes Harbor's category map only when Harbor is
installed. Reject names assigned by more than one map. Remove the SkyRL
snapshot and update callers to import each owner directly.

Shellbox requires Rigging at runtime. Harbor requires Shellbox at
runtime to read its category map.

In SkyRL, eight error names now exclude failed samples instead of
assigning zero reward. They are: RuntimeServiceError,
RuntimeLogCollectionError, EnvironmentStopError, DaytonaError,
DaytonaDockerSetupError, InternalServerError, APIConnectionError, and
APITimeoutError. Other registered names retain their SkyRL training
treatment. RetrySettings retains the existing fields and defaults.

[verifyit] Accept coin_flip probabilities within 0.1% of the reference (#12006)

`coin_flip` now scores a reply 1.0 when it is within 0.1% of the
reference probability. #11987 compared within one part in a million, so
a rounded reply scored 0 whenever the reference has more digits:
`0.07031` or `0.0703` against `0.0703125` ("exactly 7 heads in 9 fair
coin flips"). The question asks for no precision.

On the 1,000 generated `coin_flip` entries (the generator's seeds,
reasoning-gym 0.1.25), 682 references have more than four significant
figures. Entries that score 1.0:

| reply | main | this change |
|---|---|---|
| the reference | 1,000 | 1,000 |
| the reference rounded to 4 significant figures | 318 | 1,000 |
| the reference rounded to 3 significant figures | 218 | 716 |
| `0` | 0 | 0 |
| `1` | 61 | 81 |

The reference is exactly 1 on 61 entries. The 20 more that `1` gets have
references within 0.1% of 1, such as 0.9990234375 for at least one head
in ten flips. The tolerance is the one the review on #11987 suggested
(`rel_tol=1e-3`), kept in exact fractions.

`test_coin_flip_accepts_equivalent_probability` becomes three replies to
one entry: the fraction, four significant figures (0 on main) and two
significant figures (still 0).

Part of #11653

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Finish generation across decode chunks (#12018)

The inference engine could stop after prefill when the decode chunk size
(`max_rounds`) exceeded `max_seq_len`. It could also skip the final
partial chunk when `max_seq_len` was not a multiple of `max_rounds`.

Continue decoding while unfinished requests remain and each chunk makes
progress. Cap requested sequence lengths at the configured context limit
and reject prompts that leave no room for generation. The regression
test covers both truncation cases.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Preserve the full distribution at top-p one (#12010)

Keep the entire vocabulary eligible at `top_p=1`, including rows in a
batch
with lower cutoffs. The nucleus cutoff tolerance could drop a small tail
and
renormalize the remaining tokens upward, inflating the sampled token's
log
probability. Policy learning uses those scores.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Add paged generation for Snowball (#12020)

Snowball can now generate through Levanter's `InferenceEngine` with one
paged KV cache per layer. Prefill and decode follow the full forward
pass's short- and long-layer attention schedule. Padded tokens are
excluded from expert dispatch, and the sampler gathers only the logit
rows it needs.

The test compares generated token IDs and their log probabilities with a
full-sequence forward pass in single-device, tensor-parallel, and
expert-parallel configurations. The same check passed with the native
paged attention kernel on a v4 TPU mesh.

Stacked on #12019.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Add Grug attention over paged KV caches (#12019)

Snowball's short-window layers need causal sliding-window attention that
uses absolute token positions when decoding from an existing KV cache.

Add grouped-query attention over Levanter's interleaved KV pages for
batches that mix prefill and decode. Use JAX's Pallas kernel for FP32
inputs on supported TPUs and the JAX reference implementation elsewhere.
Share the TPU adapter with the existing named-axis attention path, and
let Grug rotary embeddings accept shared or per-batch absolute position
IDs.

CPU tests compare attention against a dense oracle. A v4 TPU smoke
checks standard and regrouped head layouts with static and runtime logit
scales.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[ci] Re-lock vendored SkyRL when native package floors advance (#12004)

The native package updater now re-locks each vendored project whose
`uv.lock` installs the floor owner from a local path, as well as the
root lock. Today that is `vendor/skyrl`, which installs `marin-iris`
from `lib/iris`. Each re-locked file gets the same targeted-change guard
and marker gate as the root lock, and `vendor/skyrl/uv.lock` is now on
the updater's allowlist. A failed re-lock names the lock that failed.

`vendor/skyrl/uv.lock` records the floors in `lib/iris/pyproject.toml`.
The updater re-locked only the root lock, so the vendored lock check in
`marin-lint` and `skyrl-wheel` failed on the update PR #8846.

SkyRL does not install the iris `controller` extra. Its lock records the
`marin-finelog-server` floor but does not contain the package, so the
guard now accepts a lock that never contained the released distribution.
A distribution that was locked before must still be locked at the
released version.

With the releases now on PyPI, a local `bump-releases` run changes 14
lines in `vendor/skyrl/uv.lock` and 42 in the root lock. `uv lock
--check` passes for both projects.
